purpose:
Pairs that must NEVER be named, with the evidence that condemned them. This is the negative counterpart to sibling_manual_pairs.json, which can only ADD pairs -- a wrong pair regenerates on every refresh, so the refusal has to live somewhere. Consumed by apply_sibling_annotations.py --ledger, where a rejected row is skipped (SKIP_LEDGER) however high the mapper rated it.

The approvals this file used to carry were applied on 2026-08-15 and then removed: once a name is in Ghidra, Ghidra is the record, and a stale approval list re-approves rows whose addresses have since moved. Rejections do not expire the same way -- an absent name is indistinguishable from an un-analysed one, so nothing else remembers the decision.

entries.name: core_dcube.cpp_clipTriangleToAABB_FUN_00456400
entries.note: NOT the same function. nocedit is 240 instrs calling six distinct plane clippers (MinX/MaxX/MinY/MaxY/MinZ/MaxZ); nocturne FUN_0044a150 is 786 instrs (3.5x) calling only clipEdgeToPlane. 0/6 mapped calls corroborate. Different implementation of a related idea.

entries.name: shape_multicrm.cpp_CMultiCram_getSecondModel_FUN_0053ee30
entries.note: REJECT despite an identical body: it is a generic 3-instruction accessor (return arg->field_0x8), a shape the strict hash collides on. The TUs are incompatible -- shape_multicrm.cpp is an editor-only tool, mapped into game core_stranger.cpp -- and nocedit has nothing between 005c6930 and 005c6950, so nocturne 00540a10 is most likely game-only. The body audit CANNOT see this; only the TU cross-check can.
